title: Guaranteed Serve Definitions, Credit Computation & Autoscale Interlock — Contract Draft
creator: Aisha Rao
description: Draft a contract-ready specification for Dedicated (reserved) capacity throughput guarantees that ties measurable serve definitions to a clear error-budget and crediting computation, plus an operational autoscale interlock policy. Outcome: a single reference doc and contract annex we can hand to Legal and Sales for term sheets and to Eng for implementation.
background: Enterprise customers have asked for clearer, auditable throughput guarantees that map directly to credits/compensation and operational remediation steps. Existing artifacts are fragmented (playbooks, ad-hoc emails, engineering runbooks). We need a compact, unambiguous SLA definition that covers: baseline serve bands, measurement windows, tolerated degradations, credit formulas, autoscale failure modes, and notification/appeal processes.
proposal: Deliver a contract annex with: 1) Definitions of Serve Levels (Baseline, Degraded, Critical) based on measurable serving metrics; 2) Two-tier error budget model (Throughput error budget and Latency/Availability error budget) with explicit rolling windows and quantiles; 3) A deterministic credit computation formula that scales with shortfall magnitude and duration; 4) Autoscale interlock specification describing expected autoscaler behavior, failure detection thresholds, and fallback obligations; 5) Notification, remediation SLAs, and dispute/appeal handling. Include example calculation scenarios and measurement queries for telemetry.
acceptance_criteria: Contract annex draft reviewed and accepted by Legal with at most two major change requests
Measurement queries (PromQL/SQL) included for the three primary metrics: served throughput, median latency, and 95th latency
Crediting formula validated by Finance with examples for: single-day outage, gradual degradation, and brief surge exhaustion
Engineering has an implementation plan and a list of telemetry events required to power alerts and credit computation
Sales/Customer Success sign-off on customer-facing wording for term sheets and onboarding scripts
metrics: Served TPS: tokens/sec or requests/sec served from dedicated pool (per-customer) — measured at 1s resolution and aggregated to 1m/1h
Throughput Utilization: ratio of served TPS to committed baseline TPS per AZ/region
Latency P50/P95: end-to-end request latency distribution for served requests (exclude queued requests due to throttling when explicitly applied)
Error Budget Burn Rate: ratio of shortfall-weighted time within the rolling window relative to allowed window
Autoscale Success Rate: percentage of autoscale triggers that resulted in additional capacity within defined stabilization window
credit_computation: Overview: Credits are proportional to the area under the shortfall curve. Compute shortfall as max(0, committed_throughput - observed_served_throughput). Integrate shortfall over the measurement window to get shortfall-token-hours.
Formula: Credit% = min(100, (integrated_shortfall / (committed_throughput * window_hours)) * CustomerWeightFactor) where CustomerWeightFactor defaults to 1.0 unless otherwise negotiated.

Band multipliers: Degraded band (observed >= 70% of committed) multiplier = 0.5; Critical band (observed < 70%) multiplier = 1.0. Shortfalls during scheduled maintenance excluded if announced with >72h notice.

Cap: Total credits per month capped at 100% of the monthly committed fee for the affected capacity pool unless an incident is classified as Major System Failure by Redwood and confirmed by both parties.

Example A: Single 2-hour drop from 100% to 60% on a 100k TPS commitment => shortfall = 40k TPS * 2h => integrated_shortfall=80k TPS-hours. Window=720h (30d). Credit% = (80k/(100k*720))*1.0=0.0111 => 1.11% credit of monthly fee, multiplied by critical band multiplier=1.0 => 1.11% credit.
autoscale_interlock: Expected behavior: Autoscaler should detect sustained >10% utilization above committed baseline for 5 continuous minutes and provision burst/dedicated nodes to return utilization <= target within 10 minutes.

Failure detection: If capacity increase does not reduce utilization within 15 minutes of autoscale trigger, mark autoscale as Failed and record an AutoscaleFailure telemetry event for credit computation consideration.

Compensating obligations: During verified AutoscaleFailures, Redwood will: 1) attempt cross-AZ failover if available, 2) open a high-priority incident, and 3) apply a 1.5x multiplier to shortfall during the failure window for credit computation.

Customer controls: Customers may opt-in to aggressive burst mode that prioritizes low latency over cost; contract language must call out additional charges and how credits interact with burst usage (credits computed only on dedicated baseline, not chargeable burst capacity).
notification_and_remediation: Incident detection: Telemetry will trigger internal high-priority incident when committed_throughput shortfall exceeds 10% for >10 minutes
Customer notification: Automated email + Console alert within 30 minutes of incident detection, followed by a post-incident report within 72 hours
Remediation SLA: For Critical band outages, Redwood to provide a remediation timeline and weekly status updates until resolved
Appeal process: Customers can request credit re-evaluation within 15 days with supporting telemetry; Redwood to respond within 10 business days
implementation_tasks: Define and ship new telemetry metrics: observed_served_throughput (per-customer, per-pool), autoscale_trigger, autoscale_failure
Add credit computation job that consumes 30-day rolling metrics and emits candidate credit records to Billing for review
Console UI: Add SLA status panel for Dedicated customers showing current window burn, projected credit %, and recent autoscale events
Docs & legal: Produce contract annex and short plain-language summary for sales playbook
Integration test: Simulate capacity shortfalls in staging and validate credit computation against example scenarios
risks: Measurement disagreements: differences in counting semantics (queued vs served) could lead to customer disputes
Overly generous credits: poorly calibrated multipliers could expose Redwood to outsized financial risk
Autoscaler complexity: tight autoscale interlock SLAs create engineering burden and risk of flapping if done incorrectly
Legal ambiguity: ambiguous definitions of "Major System Failure" could complicate high-stakes incidents
rollout_plan: Draft v0 for Legal and Finance review (this ticket) — target 2 weeks
Engineering scoping and telemetry sprint — 3 sprints
Pilot with two strategic customers under NDA for one month to validate measurements and credit calculations
Incorporate pilot feedback and finalize contract annex; produce standard term-sheet snippet for Sales
General availability for new Dedicated contracts after documentation and Console UI release
contract_snippets: Serve Guarantee: 'Redwood guarantees that Dedicated Serving capacity committed to Customer will be available to serve at least X requests/sec (Committed Throughput). Availability will be measured in accordance with the measurement queries provided in Appendix A.'

Credit Calculation: 'If Redwood fails to meet the Serve Guarantee, Customer will be eligible to receive service credits calculated as specified in Section 3 (Credit Computation). Credits are Customer's sole and exclusive remedy for such failures.'

Autoscale Clause: 'Redwood operates an autoscaling subsystem to maintain committed throughput. In the event the autoscaler fails to provision additional capacity as defined in the Autoscale Interlock Specification, credits will be computed with a 1.5x multiplier for the verified failure window.'
Maintenance Carveouts: 'Scheduled maintenance announced >72 hours in advance will not count towards creditable shortfall.'
